subject: Computer Networking
title: How WhatsApp Works
description: A quick win: understand How WhatsApp Works.

hook.text: Two billion users send 100 billion messages daily on WhatsApp. How does it work under the hood?

buildup.text: WhatsApp uses the Signal protocol. Every message is end-to-end encrypted with unique keys per session.

discovery.text: Messages are stored on the server only until delivered. Once received, the server copy is deleted.

twist.text: Group chats use sender keys. One encryption operation reaches all members. Efficient but less secure than 1:1.

climax.text: WhatsApp Web mirrors your phone's session. The phone must stay connected to relay messages.

punchline.text: WhatsApp encrypts everything by default. Billions trust it daily.

quiz.question: What encryption protocol does WhatsApp use?

details.summary: WhatsApp uses end-to-end encryption based on the Signal protocol to secure messages between sender and recipient. Messages travel through WhatsApp servers but are encrypted so the servers cannot read them. With over two billion users, it is the world's most popular messaging platform.
details.whyItMatters: WhatsApp proved that end-to-end encryption can work at massive scale. It made encrypted communication the default for billions of people who never chose it consciously.
takeaways: WhatsApp uses the Signal protocol for end-to-end encryption
Servers relay messages but cannot read encrypted content
Over two billion people use WhatsApp worldwide

faq.question: Can WhatsApp read your messages?
faq.answer: End-to-end encryption means messages are encrypted on your device and decrypted only on the recipient's device. WhatsApp servers cannot read message content. However, WhatsApp collects metadata: who you message, when, and how often. Metadata reveals communication patterns.

faq.question: How does WhatsApp's encryption differ from email's TLS?
faq.answer: Email TLS encrypts only between servers and each server can read the email. WhatsApp's end-to-end encryption means the message is unreadable to everyone except the sender and recipient. Even WhatsApp's own servers handle only encrypted data they cannot decrypt.
